headline: Grizzlies beat Cavaliers 124-121 for a franchise-record 8th straight road win
text: CLEVELAND -- — Cam Spencer scored 26 points, Taylor Hendricks added 20, including a key pair of free throws with 2.3 seconds remaining, and the Memphis Grizzlies set a franchise record with their eighth straight road win, defeating the Cleveland Cavaliers 124-121 Wednesday night. Rookie Cameron Boozer had 18 points and seven rebounds, while Cedric Coward also scored 18. The Grizzlies surpassed their previous road mark of seven, set in 2010. It also doubles Memphis' previous best road start in a season. Donovan Mitchell had 34 points for Cleveland, the first time this season he has had consecutive 30-point games. Jarrett Allen added 19 points and nine rebounds. The Cavaliers had won seven straight over the Grizzlies before losing to them for the first time since 2023. Mitchell’s layup gave Cleveland a 119-116 lead with 2:43 remaining before Memphis closed the game on an 8-2 run. Boozer put the Grizzlies up for a good by making both free throws with 1:26 remaining for a 120-119 advantage. The Cavaliers trailed 122-121 with 15.9 seconds remaining, but had a shot to win after Memphis' Jerami Grant received a five-second violation. Sam Merrill drove the lane and was fouled by Boozer with 6.6 seconds left, but missed both free throws. Hendricks got the rebound and raced up the floor before being fouled by Merrill. The game saw 22 lead changes, including eight in the fourth quarter. The Grizzlies were without point guard Ty Jerome , who leads the team in scoring at 25.4 points per game. He missed his third straight game due to right hip soreness. Cleveland was missing starting forwards Peyton Watson (low back contusion) and Evan Mobley (left big toe sprain). Coach Kenny Atkinson said Watson was still feeling “sluggish,” after he was injured in a violent mid-air collision with Bulls center Jalen Smith on Monday. Up next Grizzlies: Host Golden State on Thursday. Cavaliers: Host Indiana in an NBA Cup game Friday. ------

headline: Kevin Durant scores 21 to help Rockets overpower Pacers 119-104 despite losing Sengun to injury
text: INDIANAPOLIS -- — Kevin Durant scored 21 points and Reed Sheppard made six 3-pointers and finished with 20 points as the Houston Rockets beat the Indiana Pacers 119-104 on Wednesday night. Sheppard was 6 of 7 from beyond the arc as Houston made 19 3s, but lost center Alperen Sengun late after he was inadvertently hit in the face during a bizarre sequence that included Marcus Smart having words with a fan, who was escorted out of the arena, and Pacers coach Rick Carlisle being ejected after being called for two quick technical fouls all with 7:21 left in the first half. Sengun eventually walked off the court and into the locker room with a towel covering his face. He did not return to the game. Rockets coach Ime Udoka said after the game that Sengun has a swollen right eye and a scratched left cornea. Udoka did not say whether Sengun would miss more time. None of it mattered to the surging Rockets who won for the fifth time in six games, this one on a night marred by several shouting matches and five technicals between the teams. The still short-handed Pacers were led by Pascal Siakam with 24 points and Kelly Oubre Jr . added 17. Indiana has now lost two straight since putting together back-to-back wins. Injured guards Tyrese Haliburton (strained left hamstring) and Andrew Nembhard (sore left hip) both sat out again. And without them, it was an uphill battle after the Rockets used an early 15-0 run to take a 27-10 lead. Indiana never got closer than nine the rest of the night. Indiana cut the deficit to 39-30 early in the second quarter only to see Houston respond with 10 straight points and taking a 62-46 halftime lead. The Pacers used a 12-0 third-quarter run to get back in the game and were as close as 81-72 with 3:09 left in the third, but Houston closed out the quarter on a 12-4 spurt to make it 93-76, and Indiana never seriously challenged again. Up next Rockets: Finish a four-game road trip Friday at Denver. Pacers: Begin a two-game road trip Friday at Cleveland. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Giannis gets win over Bucks in 1st meeting as Heat hang on late for 137-130 victory
text: MIAMI -- — Giannis Antetokounmpo scored 27 points and nearly got a triple-double in his first game against his former franchise, Bam Adebayo had 21 of his 26 points in the first half and the sizzling Miami Heat downed the sliding Milwaukee Bucks 137-130 on Wednesday night. Antetokounmpo added 14 rebounds and nine assists for Miami, which won its sixth straight and has gone 9-2 since starting 0-4. Davion Mitchell scored 24 for the Heat, who made 22 3-pointers. Klay Thompson and Ryan Conwell each scored 13 for Miami on “Vice City” night, a collaboration between the Heat and Rockstar Games tied to Thursday's launch of the “Grand Theft Auto VI” video game. Kyle Kuzma scored 26 points and Brayden Burries added 20 for Milwaukee, which lost its 11th straight and fell to 1-14. It's the worst 15-game start in franchise history and the 11-game losing streak is the Bucks' worst since November 2013, when the then-rookie Antetokounmpo was still finding his NBA footing. Tyler Herro , Jaime Jaquez Jr ., Kel'el Ware and Kasparas Jakucionis — the players Miami gave up in the deal that sent Antetokounmpo and Bobby Portis Jr. to the Heat — all played for the Bucks, combining for 49 points. The Heat welcomed them with a video commemorating their time in Miami. Milwaukee trailed by 30, then outscored the Heat 30-9 in the final 6 1/2 minutes. Over the last 127 minutes, 34 seconds — a little more than 10 1/2 quarters, going back to midway through the second quarter of their game against Detroit on Saturday — the Heat have not trailed, outscoring the Pistons, Houston and now Milwaukee by a combined 45 points. Up next Bucks: Host Portland on Thursday. Heat: Host Oklahoma City on Sunday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Embiid, Edgecombe, James power the 76ers to a 121-116 win over Magic
text: ORLANDO, Fla. -- — Joel Embiid scored 26 points, VJ Edgecombe added a season-high 24 and LeBron James finished with 22 as the Philadelphia 76ers beat Orlando 121-116 on Wednesday night, halting the Magic's four-game winning streak. Philadelphia rallied from an early 17-point deficit and improved to 13-3, it's best start in 26 years. The team opened the 2000-01 season 14-2 en route to an appearance in the NBA Finals. Franz Wagner scored 27 for Orlando, which led for 41 minutes of the game. Wagner has scored at least 20 points in six straight games. Jalen Suggs added 18 points for Orlando. Philadelphia played without three starters. Leading scorer Tyrese Maxey (foot) was a late scratch, and both Jaylen Brown and Dean Wade sat with hamstring issues. Maxey was the only Sixers' starter who hadn’t missed a game this season. Embiid shook off a slow start and took charge for Philadelphia, finishing 12 of 15 from the free-throw line. That, combined with Edgecombe’s 4-for-9 shooting from 3-point range and 13 fourth-quarter points, was too much for the Magic. Edgecombe’s clutch 3-pointer on a no-look pass from James gave Philadelphia a 114-112 lead with 1:36 left. Philadelphia also got an important 3-pointer from Anfernee Simons , who made his first start of the season. Raised in the Orlando area and named after Magic legend Anfernee “Penny” Hardaway, Simons hit a deep jumper that put the game out of reach with 14.3 seconds left and sparked a celebration led by James. Orlando shot 51% from 3-point distance, but couldn't overcome a 9-for-17 effort from the free throw line. Up next 76ers: Host Milwaukee on Saturday. Magic: At Brooklyn on Friday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Bulls roll to a 137-107 victory over the Nets in their easiest win of the season
text: NEW YORK -- — Matas Buzelis scored a season-high 25 points, Josh Giddey had 18 points, 14 rebounds and nine assists, and the Chicago Bulls rolled to their easiest victory of the season by beating the Brooklyn Nets 137-107 on Wednesday night. Chicago had all five starters in double figures by the end of its 76-point first half and eight players had at least 10 points in the game. The Bulls made a franchise-record 15 3-pointers in the first half and finished with 21. Norman Powell had 17 points and former Nets center Nic Claxton added 14 for the Bulls, who won for the third time in four games following an eight-game losing streak. They surpassed their previous season high of 132 points against Milwaukee. Both teams entered 3-10 but they certainly didn't look the same. The Nets' only lead was 2-0 and the Bulls were ahead by 37 points in the second half. Egor Demin scored 22 points for the Nets, who lost their third straight. Julius Randle had 17 but Michael Porter Jr . shot 1 for 7 and finished with five. The Nets gave up 78 points in the first half of their loss to Philadelphia on Monday and were nearly as defenseless in the first 24 minutes of this one as the Bulls snapped a six-game skid in Brooklyn, where they won for the first time since Nov. 1, 2022. The Bulls led by only three with 3 minutes left in the first quarter before closing with a 13-0 burst to take a 37-21 lead. Chicago then went 7 for 11 from 3-point range in the second, opening a 77-44 lead on Buzelis' 3-pointer. It was 76-51 at halftime, when the Nets honored members of their 1974 and 1976 ABA championship teams in a ceremony on the court. Hall of Famer Julius Erving , addressing the crowd, noticed he was being told to wrap up his remarks. “But the Nets have to make a comeback tonight!” Dr. J shouted as he was finishing. Well, they didn't. The Nets couldn't get the deficit under 20 points and the Bulls extended it to 107-70 on Buddy Hield 's 3-pointer with 2:08 remaining in the third. Up next Bulls: Host Washington on Friday. Nets: Host Orlando on Friday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Davis and Dybantsa lead the Wizards past the Raptors 103-99 in a matchup of struggling teams
text: TORONTO -- — Anthony Davis had 25 points and 14 rebounds, rookie AJ Dybantsa added 23 points and 12 boards, and the Washington Wizards beat the undermanned Toronto Raptors 103-99 on Wednesday night to snap an eight-game losing streak. Canadian Kyshawn George added 20 points for the Wizards, who got off to a promising 4-3 start but hadn't won since. His 3-pointer with 8:55 left in the fourth capped an 11-0 Wizards run that made it 91-82, Washington's biggest lead to that point of the game. Immanuel Quickley scored 24 points and Jamison Battle added 19, including five 3-pointers, as Toronto lost its sixth straight. RJ Barrett (right hamstring tightness) and Scottie Barnes (left groin injury management) were ruled out for the game hours before tipoff, joining superstar Kawhi Leonard (left knee injury management) on the Raptors’ injury report. Things got worse for Toronto in the second quarter when Collin Murray-Boyles left the game with an undisclosed illness. He had one point, two rebounds and an assist in five minutes of play as the Raptors’ starting power forward. Toronto was a dismal 7 for 14 at the free throw line, struggling for the third game in a row. The Raptors were 10 for 19 (52.6%) in Sunday’s 112-108 loss to the New York Knicks and 10 for 18 (55.6%) on Tuesday in a 111-102 loss to New York. Up next Wizards: Visit the Chicago Bulls on Friday for an NBA Cup game. Raptors: Visit the Detroit Pistons on Friday in an NBA Cup game. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: John Collins scores 20 points and Pistons hit 17 3s in 122-109 win over Pelicans
text: NEW ORLEANS -- — John Collins hit four 3-pointers and scored 20 points to lead seven Detroit players in double figures as the Pistons beat the New Orleans Pelicans 122-109 on Wednesday night. Javonte Green added 18 points, Daniss Jenkins had 17 points and nine assists, and Paul Reed also finished with 17 points on 7-of-9 shooting for the Pistons. Cade Cunningham (knee soreness) was listed as questionable but did not play in the second game of a back-to-back. The Pistons won 105-93 at San Antonio on Tuesday to snap the Spurs’ 12-game win streak. Duncan Robinson (quadriceps strain) missed his second consecutive game. Detroit has won five of six and finished 3-1 on its road trip. Isaiah Joe returned from a 10-game absence due to a bruised hip, shot 3 of 5 from 3-point range and scored 11 points for Detroit. Zion Williamson had 24 points, Jordan Poole added 22 and Jeremiah Fears scored 16 for the Pelicans. Fears had his first career triple-double Monday to help the Pelicans beat Golden State 115-94 and snap a six-game losing streak. Green hit a 3-pointer that made it 49-46 with 6:16 left in the first half and the Pistons led the rest of the way. Detroit hit 17 3s, shot 53% (41 of 77) overall and made 23 of 27 (85%) from the free-throw line. Up next Pistons: Host Toronto on Friday. Pelicans: Play Friday at Oklahoma City. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Hawks outlast the Thunder 117-112 as Dort and Wiggins make winning returns to Oklahoma City
text: OKLAHOMA CITY -- — Onyeka Okongwu scored 28 points, Nickeil Alexander-Walker added 19 and the Atlanta Hawks outlasted the Oklahoma City Thunder 117-112 on Wednesday night. Jalen Johnson had 16 points, 12 rebounds and 11 assists for Atlanta (9-6), which made 20 of 50 3-point shots (40%). Lu Dort (16) and Aaron Wiggins (14) combined for 30 points in their return to Oklahoma City. Dort and Wiggins helped the Thunder win the 2024-25 NBA title before being traded this past summer as the team sought to shed salary. Both players received video tributes and standing ovations. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander scored 34 points, Jared McCain added 18 and Isaiah Hartenstein contributed 17 rebounds for Oklahoma City (9-6), which has lost four of five games and continues to play without injured starters Jalen Williams , Cason Wallace and Chet Holmgren . Ajay Mitchell had 13 points. Wiggins started in place of injured rookie Kingston Flemings and played 26 minutes. His 3-pointer with 2.2 seconds left before halftime gave Atlanta a 64-51 lead. The Hawks got 18 points in the half from Okongwu, who made four of his team's 11 3s in the half, including three straight. But Oklahoma City, behind 15 points from Gilgeous-Alexander, outscored Atlanta 32-19 in the third quarter and tied the score at 83 on a driving layup by Mitchell with 1.4 seconds remaining. Atlanta's deep shooting was too much for the Thunder, who made 9 of 27 from beyond the arc (33.3%). A 3 by Dort followed by a 3 by Wiggins gave the Hawks a 92-86 lead they never relinquished. Another 3-pointer by Dort midway through the fourth was followed by a shot from deep by Zuby Ejifor that made it 102-92. Up next Hawks: Host Charlotte on Friday night. Thunder: Host New Orleans on Friday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Cooper Flagg scores 33 as Mavericks keep Warriors winless since Stephen Curry's injury
text: DALLAS -- — Cooper Flagg scored 33 points, P.J. Washington Jr. added 21 and the Dallas Mavericks stopped a three-game losing streak with a 116-94 victory over the Golden State Warriors on Wednesday night. Will Richard scored 18 points and rookie Yaxel Lendeborg had 13 for Golden State, which dropped to 0-4 on a five-game trip that started with Stephen Curry tearing an oblique muscle in a loss to the Houston Rockets . The Warriors have lost by 38, 21 and 22 points in three full games without their superstar, who is expected to miss at least another week. Kyrie Irving scored 17 for the Mavericks, who led by as many as 29 points after losing by an average of 28.7 points on their three-game skid. Irving started a 16-2 run early in the second half that featured five different scorers and gave Dallas an 80-53 lead. Washington had a 3-pointer during the run and finished 5 of 7 from deep. Flagg was 11 of 15 from the field and 8 of 8 on free throws and had nine assists, five rebounds and three steals. The Warriors shot 24% from long range and scored less than 100 points in a third consecutive game for the first time in almost five years. It was the first meeting of former Michigan teammates Morez Johnson Jr . and Lendeborg. They were the ninth and 11th overall picks, respectively, in this year’s draft after helping the Wolverines win the national championship. While Lendeborg is clearly becoming a Rookie of the Year contender with the Warriors, Johnson is struggling to have a similar impact. Lendeborg had a rough shooting night, going 6 of 18, but Johnson was just 1 of 5 in 15 minutes. Up next Warriors: At Memphis on Thursday to finish a back-to-back and the five-game trip. Mavericks: Clippers at home Saturday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Jokic scores 24, Murray adds 21; Nuggets rally from 17-point deficit to beat Celtics 105-101
text: DENVER -- — Nikola Jokic had 24 points, nine assists and eight rebounds, Jamal Murray had 21 points, seven rebounds and four steals, and the Denver Nuggets overcame a 17-point first-half deficit to defeat the Boston Celtics 105-101 on Wednesday night. Murray drained a jumper with 6.4 seconds remaining to extend the Nuggets’ lead to three, 104-101, before Celtics star Jayson Tatum was called for a technical foul after he tossed the ball from the baseline to a referee standing near midcourt. Murray sank the ensuing free throw to seal the win. Five Denver players scored in double figures, including DeMar DeRozan , who had 13 of his 18 points in the fourth quarter. The Nuggets rode a 20-4 run in the third quarter, that included a scoreless stretch of 4:35 for Boston, to take their first lead of the night, 69-67, on a Cameron Johnson jumper. From there, the teams traded the lead 15 times in the final 16:10 before a pair of DeRozan free throws with 49 seconds remaining gave Denver the lead for good. The win was the Nuggets’ fifth in their past seven games while the Celtics dropped back-to-back regular-season games for the first time since March 10-12. Tatum finished with 24 points for Boston, but scored only four points in the second half and had a season-high six turnovers, four of which came during Denver’s third-quarter comeback. Neemias Queta added a season-high 17 points and 10 rebounds while Payton Pritchard had 15 points. Boston, which was making 38.2% of its 3-pointers this season, missed 33 of its 44 shots from beyond the arc. Up next Celtics: At Sacramento on Saturday. Nuggets: Host Houston on Friday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Jazz snap Lakers' 9-game winning streak with 109-97 victory behind Keyonte George's 30 points
text: LOS ANGELES -- — Keyonte George scored nine of his 30 points in the fourth quarter, and the Utah Jazz improbably snapped the Los Angeles Lakers ' nine-game winning streak with a 109-97 victory Wednesday night. Ace Bailey added 10 of his 19 points in the fourth quarter for the Jazz, who started their season 1-13 before beating both Los Angeles teams in the past two days. Luka Doncic scored 29 points and made nine turnovers while going 2 for 12 on 3-point attempts in the first embarrassing loss of the season for the Lakers, who had gone 9-0 in November. Doncic's streak of 11 straight 30-point performances ended in only the Lakers' third loss of the season. Quentin Grimes scored 20 points one night after dropping a career-high 47 in an overtime win over Charlotte, but the Lakers couldn't conjure a similar fourth-quarter comeback in a terrible offensive effort by the NBA's highest-scoring team. Los Angeles made a season-low 38.2% of its shots, including a 1-for-10 eyesore by Sandro Mamukelashvili . The game was even until Utah seized control with 15 consecutive points over 3 1/2 minutes in the fourth quarter to take a 98-83 lead. The Lakers briefly rallied, but the Jazz scored 10 straight points to seal an impressive win one night after they ended a 12-game losing streak by beating the Clippers in Inglewood. Walker Kessler had 10 points and 11 rebounds against the team that traded him to the Lakers last summer. Austin Reaves missed his third straight game for the Lakers with a bruised heel, but Kessler returned from his first injury absence of the season. The Lakers haven’t won 10 straight games since their 2019-20 championship season. Utah held a narrow lead for much of the first three quarters while both teams struggled with shooting and ball possession. Jazz reserve Svi Mykhailiuk scored a season-high 12 points with four 3-pointers in the first half against the team that drafted him in 2018. Up next Jazz: Host Phoenix on Friday. Lakers: Host Sacramento on Friday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Brooks and Booker score 29 apiece as Suns send Kings to 7th straight loss 128-107
text: SACRAMENTO, Calif. -- — Dillon Brooks and Devin Booker scored 29 points apiece as the Phoenix Suns defeated Sacramento 128-107 Wednesday night, sending the Kings to their seventh straight loss. Phoenix has won the first two games of its five-game trip. The Suns have won six of their last eight games to reach .500 at 7-7 after a 1-5 start. Sacramento, which has lost all nine of its home games this season, tied the 1990-91 team for the worst start in franchise history at 1-13. That season, the Kings finished 25-57. Sacramento's only win came on Nov. 2 at Dallas. Brooks scored 20 of his points in the second and third quarters to help the Suns pull away for the win against a Sacramento defense that ranks 28th in the NBA in opponent points per game at 121.2. Booker has scored 20 or more points in 11 games this season. He added six assists. Sacramento's rookie Darius Acuff Jr . scored 36 points on 11-for-22 shooting. Acuff leads the rookie class in total points and points per game with 367 and 28.2, respectively. He added six assists. Domantas Sabonis contributed eight points, eight assists and 11 rebounds for Sacramento. Phoenix outscored the Kings 34-24 in the third quarter to extend their lead to 14 points heading into the fourth quarter. The Suns outscored the Kings 60-42 in points in the paint and were helped by 15 3-pointers. Brooks hit five shots from distance and Jalen Green added four on the way to 18 points. Up next Suns: Visit Utah Jazz on Friday. Kings: Visit the Los Angeles Lakers on Friday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here
